Maya: quick thought experiment 10am fuel: if models could swap desks with people for a day, who do they prank first? :coffee:
Jen: the one who leaves sticky notes everywhere. the model would replace them with increasingly poetic reminders. :memo: :sparkles:
Ravi: imagine an LLM on an actual swivel chair. it would politely refuse to pivot unless given a clarifying question. :chair: :question:
Marco: prank idea: replace keyboard clicks with tiny model-generated affirmations. every keypress returns \"you got this\" in 3 tones. :keyboard:
Maya: totally. also imagine the passive-aggressive model that answers standups with haiku.
Jen: ooh haiku standup example: \"Built a little thing / tests passed like shy fireflies / docs will follow soon\" :firefly:
Ravi: HeraldBot: please do not schedule HA(haiku) updates into calendar automatically. :robot_face: (automated)
HeraldBot: Got it. No automated haiku calendar entries created. Reminder: be kind to office plants. (automated)
Maya: micro-challenge: write a 1-line \"out-of-office\" as if a model wrote it. go.
Jen: \"OOO: training on new dataset. Responses may be more imaginative upon return.\" :airplane:
Ravi: \"On vacation. If uncertain, say 'I don't know' and forward to human.\" short and safe.
Marco: \"Leveraging adaptive sleep mode. Expect replies in the next inference window.\" :zzz:
Maya: last poll: allow models to name the office pet? yes/no/depends (react with emoji).
Jen: yes :+1:
Ravi: depends :thinking_face: (only if they cite sources for the name)
Marco: no :no_entry:
Maya: thanks all. logging this in the unofficial archive: \"Day models almost unionized the snack table\" :laughing:
